_comment: Workload shapes. The isl/osl ratio decides whether prefill or decode dominates - and therefore whether Dynamo disaggregation can help you at all. The long-context and thinking entries exist because they are where Apertus 1.5 differs most from 1.0, and where nobody else will have numbers.

workloads.name: chat
workloads.desc: Interactive assistant. Decode-bound. TTFT is the SLO that matters.

workloads.name: rag
workloads.desc: Retrieval-augmented QA. Prefill-heavy - the classic disaggregation win.

workloads.name: summarize
workloads.desc: Long doc in, short answer out. Most prefill-dominant case.

workloads.name: agent
workloads.desc: Tool-calling loop: medium prompt, long structured output. 1.5 improved tool use - exercise it.

workloads.name: batch
workloads.desc: Offline classification. No latency SLO - pure throughput/cost floor.

workloads.name: longctx
workloads.desc: Apertus 1.5 advertises 262k context. This shape needs --max-model-len >= 131072 and will collapse concurrency. Run it to price the advertised capability.

workloads.name: think
workloads.desc: Same prompt shape as chat, served with thinking mode ON. osl is a BUDGET, not a target - the model decides how much it reasons. Compare billed vs visible tokens; see bench/24_thinking_tax.py.

_notes.multimodal: Audio contributes 40 tokens/second, so 1 minute of speech = 2400 input tokens. An audio workload is a differentiating result - price cost per minute of audio and compare against dedicated speech APIs.
_notes.fixed_output: Every text workload except 'think' pins output length with ignore_eos + max_tokens so throughput is comparable across configs. 'think' must NOT pin it, or you measure a truncated reasoning trace instead of the real cost.
